body:
@DarioSamo, as you suggested, I introduced a new resource usage (`ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_INPUT`).
Then, I had to update the demo and the renderer branch splitting the raytracing list in 3 parts: 
1. Build BLASs
2. Build TLAS
3. Trace rays

So 1 generates inputs for 2, and 2 generate inputs for 3, while proper memory barriers are inferred. With this, I removed the explicit barriers mentioned in the comment above.
@DarioSamo, new version, I guess this fits better in the draw graph. I introduced a new build acceleration command, as you suggested, separated from the "list".
Seems good, although TYPE_BUILD_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE seems to remain on RaytracingListInstruction and is probably meant to be removed.

Given `add_acceleration_structure_build` will likely be called per frame, you should avoid the allocations using Vector<> here and instead use a thread_local LocalVector that gets resized to the correct size and filled in each frame instead.
VectorView is preferred for the input here so we don't impose which type of Vector we allow as the input.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100399

`_check_transfer_worker_buffer` must be called on all relevant buffers used during construction of these structures. That goes for the transform buffer and the buffers used by the vertex and index array. This method is called to ensure the data upload from asynchronous sources is finished before the commands from this frame are processed.
Given TLAS creation will be already a bit of a hot path when it concerns allocation per frame, we should be using `thread_local` on this vector with a resize operation instead.

These are currently misplaced, as the check must be performed during the actual BLAS/TLAS building, not during the creation of the BLAS/TLAS driver resource. That way the check is deferred as much as possible until the acceleration structure is actually built.
Same reasoning as everywhere else, `thread_local` or ALLOCA must be used on hot paths such as these (preferrably TLS as it won't blow up if it runs out of stack memory).

Considering the awkwardness of this implementation, I think it'd be warranted that we make up a fake new type of barrier specifically for acceleration structures.

From the driver's abstraction side, we identify buffers, textures and AS as separate entities. That'd allow each back-end to have an easier time implementing the synchronization primitives required for it.

Support for BLAS and TLAS creation is not linked to pipeline support. It should check if query **or** pipeline are supported on these cases. Raytracing lists are the only ones where SUPPORTS_RAYTRACING_PIPELINE is a requirement.
We'll postpone it.
Updated both the check and the enum name to `SUPPORTS_RAY_QUERY`
